_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II: Siyawush cycle — Sudaba's lust, the fire-ordeal. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.zh: 蘇達貝之慾與西亞瓦什之拒

region.zh: 卡烏斯後宮（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Siyawush secs. 6-7

summary.en: Sudaba, the Shah's wife, beholds the peerless prince and grows distraught; her secret envoy is rebuffed — I am no chamberer, or given to romances and intrigues — so she beguiles Kaus into sending the youth to the women's bower to visit his sisters. She descends her golden throne, embraces him long and kisses his eyes, and Siyawush, knowing well what that love meant and that such fondness was not in the way of God, goes quickly to his sisters instead. When the Shah asks her judgment of Siyawush, her malice takes another turn.
summary.zh: 王后蘇達貝一見無雙王子便神魂顛倒；密使遭拒——「我非狎邪之徒」——她遂哄騙卡烏斯讓王子入後宮探望姐妹。她自金座降下，久久擁抱、吻其眉眼；西亞瓦什深知此情有悖神道，徑往姐妹處。當王問她對西亞瓦什的評價時，她的惡意另闢蹊徑。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Potiphar's-wife motif. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Time passed, the Shah still joyed in Siyawush, till as they sat one day Sudaba entered, beheld the prince's face, and grew distraught. Her heart throbbed; she is wasted to a thread, thou wouldst have said, or ice before the fire. She bade one go by stealth to him and say: 'twould cause no wonder if thou shouldest visit the royal bower anon. The envoy went, but noble Siyawush was wroth and said: entice me not. I am no chamberer, or given to romances and intrigues.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Another day at dawn Sudaba sought the Shah and said: the sun and moon have never seen thy peer or any like thy son. Send him to thy bower to see his sisters and thy favourites, whose hearts are full, whose cheeks are wet with yearning. The Shah replied: thou sayest right; thou hast a hundred mothers' love for him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The prince suspected that his father sought to prove him, for Kai Kaus was knowing and smooth-tongued, wise, shrewd of heart, and ready to distrust. But in the women's quarters of the Shah what shall I learn? Yet if so the Shah commandeth my custom henceforth is to visit them. When Hirbad held up the veil that hung before the door the mind of Siyawush foreboded ill.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush secs. 6-7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Now Siyawush on entering the bower beheld a brightly shining, golden throne where sat moon-faced Sudaba, like Paradise itself in hue and perfume. When Siyawush appeared within the veil Sudaba hastened to descend the throne, advanced with graceful gait, embraced him long, long kissed his eyes and face. Now Siyawush knew well what that love meant, and that such fondness was not in the way of God, and, since it was unseemly there, went quickly to his sisters, who enthroned him with many a blessing on a golden seat.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Siyawush sec. 13

summary.en: To purge foul surmise, Kaus has a hundred caravans of camels gather firewood till two huge mountains rise on the plain, pours black naphtha over all, and has the heaps fired: the earth became more radiant than the sky. Siyawush comes forth in golden helmet and white raiment, sprinkles camphor over himself as bodies are prepared for burial, prays the Judge that hath no needs to grant him a passage through this mount of fire, and urges his black steed on like smoke. The flames close over his head; the noble hero reappears with rosy cheeks and smiles upon his lips — had flame been water he had not been wetted — and the people cry: God hath shown mercy to the innocent.
summary.zh: 為洗清誣告，卡烏斯令百隊駱駝運柴，壘成兩座柴山，澆以黑石腦油，點火焚天——大地比天空還亮。西亞瓦什金盔白衣、撒聖樟腦（如為身後事妝扮），祈求無所求的裁決者賜他穿越火山之路，縱黑駒如煙而入。烈焰吞沒其頂；英雄卻面頰緋紅、唇含笑意而現——火若為水，衣不沾濕——萬民歡呼：「神憐惜無辜者！」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the fire-ordeal is a Zoroastrian juridical motif. No living community restriction.

passages.text: He gave instructions to his minister to have a hundred caravans of camels brought from the plain. These went to gather firewood, while all the people of Iran looked on, till two huge mountains rose that might be seen two leagues away. They piled two mounts of firewood on the plain while all the folk looked on; a path was left such that a horseman armed might hardly pass between the piles. This done, the glorious Shah bade pour black naphtha over all the wood, and ten score men came to light and blow the fire.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: When first they blew there was a mass of smoke, but presently the tongues of fire rose fast; the earth became more radiant than the sky, the people shouted and the flames ascended. All that were on the plain were scorched and wept to see the cheery face of Siyawush, who came before his sire with golden helmet and raiment all of white. His mien was tranquil, his face all smiles, his heart all hopefulness; his black steed's hoofs sent dust up to the moon.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The prince then sprinkled camphor o'er himself, so bodies are prepared for burial, and lighting from his charger did obeisance. Be not discomfited, said Siyawush, that fortune taketh such a turn as this. I am dishonoured: such a state is ruin. If I am innocent I shall escape, while if in fault the Maker will not heed me; but by the power of God who giveth good I shall not feel the heat. As he drew near the flames he prayed the Judge that hath no needs: grant me a passage through this mount of fire, and free me from my sire's misprision.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Then urged he his black steed on like smoke; a wail ascended from the city and the waste. From every side the flames closed o'er his head, and none could see his helmet or his horse, while all the plain wept tears of blood. The noble hero nathless reappeared with rosy cheeks and smiles upon his lips; a roar went up as men caught sight of him: the young Shah cometh from the fire! Had flame been water he had not been wetted, his garments would have holden none of it, for when all-holy God doth so vouchsafe the breath of fire is even as the wind; there was universal joy, and each to other gave the gladsome tidings: God hath shown mercy to the innocent.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 13 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Siyawush Begs Sudaba's Life, and Is Repaid in Sorcery
title.zh: 西亞瓦什為蘇達貝求情卻遭暗算

region.zh: 卡烏斯王庭（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Siyawush sec. 14

summary.en: Kaus, ox-head mace in hand, condemns Sudaba to the gibbet for treacherously seeking his son's life and exposing him to fire. The Iranians say the punishment for her is death, but Siyawush pleads: pardon for my sake Sudaba's fault; she may be warned and walk advisedly — for if she perish by his hand he will be sorry for it in the end. The Shah grants mercy, Sudaba returns to the palace, and, by secret sorceries, works on Kaus to ruin Siyawush according to the evil of her nature; the Shah becomes mistrustful through her talk but speaks not aught thereof to any one.
summary.zh: 卡烏斯手持牛首錘，判蘇達貝絞刑——她陰謀害子、縱火試煉。群臣皆言當死，西亞瓦什卻代為求情：「饒她一命吧，願她引以為戒。」（他心想：若她死於父親之手，父親終將悔恨，反倒怨我。）王允其所請；蘇達貝重返後宮，暗中以妖術蠱惑王心圖謀害西亞瓦什；王漸生疑忌，卻不對任何人言明。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: Kaus the fourth day sat upon the throne of kings; an ox-head mace was in his hand. Fierce in his wrath he had Sudaba summoned before him, told her what had passed, and said: thou art a shameless woman! What part is this that thou hast played throughout in treacherously seeking my son's life, in causing him to be exposed to fire? No excuses will now avail thee; thou art not fit to live.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The great Shah asked the Iranians: for the evil that she hath done by stealth, what shall I do? All did obeisance and said: the punishment for her is death; she ought to suffer for her evil deeds. He bade the deathsman: hang her in the street upon the gibbet and be pitiless. At her abandonment the women wailed, and Shah Kaus was sorrowful of heart.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Let not thy heart be troubled, said Siyawush, but pardon for my sake Sudaba's fault; she may be warned and walk advisedly. For, he thought, if she perish by his hand he will be sorry for it in the end, and see in me the author of his grief. The Shah, who had been seeking some excuse for mercy, answered him: I grant thee this because I see that right was on thy side.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: When Siyawush had kissed his father's throne he brought back Sudaba and escorted her home to the palace by the Shah's command. Now in time the heart of Shah Kaus so warmed to her that he could not forbear to eye her face in love, while, for her part, by secret sorceries she worked on him to ruin Siyawush according to the evil of her nature. The Shah became mistrustful through her talk, but spake not aught thereof to any one.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Siyawush sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
